title.narrative: Activity under preparation Global Gateway Investments on Energy Transition with Bolivia. Implementation and expansion phase (Phase II). Component 2. Energy Transition with Bolivia (GIZ)

description.narrative: Bolivia is one of the countries with the highest levels of solar radiation in the world with the Altiplano region exhibiting the highest average. This presents a unique opportunity to reduce its over-reliance on hydrocarbons which is at the source of its macroeconomic deficit as well as to advance in the decarbonisation of its electricity mix. The EU support to the overall programme ¿Energy Transition with Bolivia¿ through 2024-2027 envisages an EU grant contribution of up to EUR 27M, out of which EUR 5M have been already mobilised under the AAP-2024 for Phase I. Phase II, under the AAP-2025, proposes an EU grant of EUR 16M, and an indicative EUR 6M may be used for Phase III under the AAP-2026 or 2027, depending on the outcomes of lithium investments preparation. Action 1 continues the logic initiated in 2024 with Phase I, combining investments mostly in solar and a contingency for emerging needs on lithium allowing Team Europe to respond swiftly to a now rapidly evolving race with Russian and Chinese competitors. This represents a modular asymmetric approach, which depends on how the lithium component evolves. For energy projects to be effective, the governance and legal grounds for investments need to be sufficiently prepared. To contribute towards this goal, Action 1 includes an allocation for further technical assistance. Accordingly, Action 1 involves two components:Component 1 foresees a EUR 12M investment grant to move forward to Phase II (implementation) of the 2024 ¿LACIF Energy Transition Programme in Bolivia (Phase I)¿, jointly with AFD and the EIB. The corresponding Delegation Agreement for phase I is about to be signed, involving an initial EU contribution of EUR 5M for Technical Assistance preparatory activities (EUR 3.6 for solar and EUR 1.4 for lithium). The top-up of EUR 12M, mostly for investment grants, will allow to move into the implementation phase of the programme, in line with the original project plan.. Component 1 will continue to be led by AFD, with a EUR 100M loan and a EUR 0,7M AFD grant to carry out hydrogeological studies, and a EUR 70M loan from the EIB. This may be complemented by up to EUR 10M in debt swaps from Spain whereby the Government will invest that money where required for the programme.Component 1 will consist of providing loans and investment grants to finance the construction of two solar plants, one in Vinto (132 MW) and another one in Santiváñez (66 MW). Contingent on the progress in the lithium development during Phase IIthe EIB would consider expanding the loan from EUR 70M to up to EUR 320M and AFD may also expand its loan. In such scenario, part of the 16M in investment grants may be used for the lithium component in combination with these loans, and a further 6M in investment grants could be mobilised in AAP 2026/27. Team Europe started engaging in lithium only in early 2023 when Chinese and Russian companies had already qualified under the first call for proposals by the Government of Bolivia (¿convocatorias¿) when no EU companies had even applied. By 2025, four EU companies have already `qualified¿ for lithium extraction and production and are ready to sign contracts with the Bolivian Government. To be noted that to meet EU Battery passport environmental standards, a significant input of solar energy is likely to be necessary for lithium carbonate production.
